\s[0]Camera Zoom: \c[3]\v[tmp.cameraZoom]%\c[0]
Player timescale: \c[3]\v[tmp.timescale]%\c[0]
Slow motion time factor: \c[3]\v[tmp.slowMotion]%\c[0]

\s[0]\c[3]Timescale\c[0] only affects a specific entity. It throttles the timeflow speed at which all their actions and animations play out. This menu can be used to apply a timescale to the \c[3]player\c[0].

A timescale reduction is what the \c[3]chill\c[0] status applies. Conversely, the Triblader art \i[element-shock]\c[3]Overclock\c[0] and Hexacast art \i[element-wave]\c[3]Temporal Miasma\c[0] grant a timeflow increase.

\s[0]In addition to the player themselves, timescale only affects proxies and effects that are \c[3]time-attached\c[0]. All BALL and STONE proxies are \c[3]time-detached\c[0], along with any GENERIC proxies that are set to \c[3]"timeDisconnect": true\c[0] or that use the \c[3]DETACH_TIME_PARENT\c[0] action step.

Usually, \c[3]time-attached\c[0] GENERIC proxies are utilized in tandem with player action sequences. One example is the laser in Lea's \i[element-heat]\c[3]Flare Burn!\c[0]. GENERIC proxies that are free-moving projectiles or buffs (not involved in a player action sequence in tandem with the player) are usually \c[3]time-detached\c[0].

\s[0]Unlike timescale, \c[3]Slow Motion\c[0] affects all entities EXCEPT for the one creating the slow motion and any \c[3]time-attached\c[0] proxies \c[3]they\c[0] own. \c[3]Time-attached\c[0] proxies belonging to other entities are slowed, along with ALL \c[3]time-detached\c[0] proxies regardless of owner.

An example is how Lea's \i[element-shock]\c[3]Song of Storms\c[0] slows down time for all entities except Lea (the entity creating the slow motion) and the shock clone (a time-attached GENERIC proxy used in tandem with the player during the combo).

\s[0]Because \c[3]Slow Motion\c[0] slows all \c[3]time-detached\c[0]  proxies, it is unlike \c[3]timescale\c[0] which NEVER has an effect on these proxies. This is why normal ranged shots (which are BALL proxies, and all BALL proxies are time-detached) are slowed down when you shoot them during \i[element-shock]\c[3]Glitch Time\c[0], in which your own slow motion is active.

\s[0]The slow motion settings in this menu work by commanding an invisible enemy in the room to apply slow motion, just like Lea does during Song of Storms. The result is that you, the player, are slowed down along with all your proxies. It doesn't matter whether any of your proxies are time-attached or not because none of them belong to the invisible entity who is creating the slow motion.

Again, only \c[3]time-attached\c[0] proxies that \c[3]belong\c[0] to the entity creating the slow motion are immune from the slowdown.
